title: Emrys and the Vector
premise: Mirabel Eriksen, exiled xenolinguist of the forgotten colony Vesper Hollow, has spent nine years recording its slow suffocation while Earth's transmission loop decays into static. When a distress call arrives in Ashkari—a language extinct for two centuries—she realizes the colony's founders were survivors of a genocide Earth erased from its records, and that two approaching fleets, one human and one Ashkari remnant, are converging on the truth. To prevent a war neither side can afford, Mirabel must keep alive the founding lie that the colonists are Ashkari descendants, translating herself into a heritage she never had. In the end, she broadcasts the real records alongside her fabricated bridge-language, letting both fleets choose memory over vengeance—and chooses to remain on dying Vesper Hollow as its last voice, finally dreaming in a language that is hers because she made it so.
about_author: Felix Vasquez is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing dying dialects for archival projects before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town where, he claims, the fog still carries signals no one sent.

chapters.title: The Quiet Census
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She records the colony's 214 remaining souls and their fading dialects, establishing her ritual of documenting what no one will read. The emotional beat is tender resignation—she loves these people by cataloguing their endings.

chapters.title: Static Where Home Used to Be
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Earth's final scheduled transmission loop degrades mid-broadcast; the colony learns officially that they are forgotten. Governor Ansel demands she keep it secret to prevent panic. Beat: betrayal dressed as protection.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, night shift. A distress signal arrives in Ashkari, a language she knows only from forbidden colonial archives. She answers in broken Ashkari before she can stop herself. Beat: electric terror and longing—the first conversation in years.

chapters.title: What the Founders Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating Mirabel and young archivist Teo's POV. They excavate the sealed first-generation records: the colonists were Ashkari refugees given human identities. Beat: vertigo of inheritance—everything Mirabel believed about home dissolves.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on One Horizon
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Long-range scopes confirm a human punitive fleet and an Ashkari remnant fleet both inbound, each believing the other destroyed the original colony ships. Beat: dread; the lie of identity is now the only firewall.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Lies
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Under Ansel's orders, she constructs a false origin narrative in fluent Ashkari, teaching the colonists their invented ancestry. Some embrace it fervently; Teo refuses. Beat: complicity curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Starlight
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Ashkari vanguard lands; their commander, Sef-Ilan, interviews her in the old tongue and senses seams in her story. Their charged exchange becomes mutual recognition of two people keeping dead things alive. Beat: intimacy inside deception.

chapters.title: The Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs as the human fleet arrives demanding surrender and proof of lineage. Ansel plans to sacrifice Teo as a scapegoat for the archives' falsification. Beat: panic; loyalty and truth pull Mirabel apart at the seam.

chapters.title: Everything True, Everything Ours
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. She hijacks the colony's transmitter and broadcasts the genuine genocide records plus her hybrid bridge-language, forcing both fleets to hear the same grief simultaneously. Beat: cathartic exposure—she burns the lie to save everyone it protected.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue a year later. Fleets withdrawn, joint memorial established, most colonists relocated—but Mirabel stays with a handful who choose the colony over rescue, teaching children the new language. Beat: quiet peace; survival's price paid willingly, inheritance rewritten as choice.
